name: Rendak Sorrel-Hibiscus Fruit Leathers
description: Thin, rollable fruit leathers made from synth-sorrel and hibiscus concentrate, with a tartness that fades into a floral sweetness. Each sheet is 30cm long, sold in a paper scroll tube.
flavor_profile: Sharp, cranberry-adjacent sorrel tartness giving way to hibiscus floral notes — long, dry finish with a hint of citrus peel
cultural_context: Rendak Fruit Leathers are ubiquitous in Tier 1 school environments — cheap, filling enough to take the edge off hunger, and durable enough to survive a day in a bag. The scroll tube has become a minor craft medium among Shelf youth, who paint or draw on them before selling them as micro-art objects in informal markets.
story_hooks: A Shelf school has banned Rendak Fruit Leathers after a rumor spreads that the latest batch contains trace appetite suppressants — parents are furious, the company denies it, but the rumor has a source that knows something real.
The scroll tube art micro-market has inadvertently become a communication network for a youth resistance group — the illustrations on sold tubes contain encoded location and meeting data.

Kalvex Nutrition is quietly reformulating Rendak Fruit Leathers to reduce cost, which will eliminate the real hibiscus extract and replace it with a synthetic analog — a food journalist embedded in the Shelf is about to break the story.
